uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it moves rate expectations and the pound; the September figure also sets benefit uprating.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists warned this month that UK inflation would reach 5% if a US diesel ban goes ahead, a threat aimed straight at the fuel that moves British freight. This September figure is the baseline before any such ban bites, and it is also the reading that benefits and pensions are uprated by.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee is split: hiring stalled at 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected, yet inflation has topped its target for 5.5 years and most officials expect another hike by year-end. Trump's panel on removing Governor Lisa Cook adds a fight over who sits at the table.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, after a hike officials called proportionate, and Wunsch says the ECB will probably have to hike again. Patsalides warns higher rates can't prevent more shocks, and Moulin says France needs no rescue yet. Governments must nominate Isabel Schnabel's successor by 28 October, the day before.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, the threshold its caution on rates has long rested on. Wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September, and yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago as a weak yen compounds the oil shock. Japanese yields have already jumped.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The Bank of England's committee decides whether to hold or move its policy rate, which settles what households and firms borrowing from banks pay into the new year.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials have said they expect another hike by year-end, but the Labor Department's count of 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected split them, with inflation above target for 5.5 years. The committee weighs that while Trump moves to remove Lisa Cook and demands Powell resign.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency has pushed to hold the G20 to its original priorities, and Russia's sherpa has publicly backed that push. This summit settles how far the host narrows the agenda, and whether the other members sign a joint statement on those terms.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2% while business activity hit a 3½-year high, so this meeting weighs whether the September hike was enough. Wunsch says another will probably be needed; Patsalides that higher rates can't prevent more shocks. Isabel Schnabel's successor is nominated by 28 October.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: This is the committee's last vote of the year, and it settles the cost of borrowing that households and firms carry into the new year.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September and yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more, as an oil shock routed through the Strait of Hormuz compounds a weak yen. Three sources say the Bank of Japan is weighing whether to declare underlying inflation at its 2% goal, the judgement its case for a rate rise turns on.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what US households pay for a basket of goods and services. It is the inflation reading that moves Treasury yields, the dollar and expectations for Fed rates.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end, but the committee is split, and Warsh has drawn IMF praise for putting price stability first. Today's release is the figure that argument turns on: whether the Hormuz oil shock is staying in fuel or spreading into everything else US households buy.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Producer Price Index, which tracks what US producers receive for their goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop prices, and bond yields move with it.
fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the latest US PPI reading. It will show how far price pressure has built up in the supply chain before it reaches shoppers.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what US stores, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so the figure moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.recent: The Census Bureau publishes US retail sales, settling how much consumers spent at retailers and restaurants last month. It is the first hard spending figure for the month.
